Definition: properly, to pale, i.e. by implication to be ashamed; also (by implication) to be disappointed or delayed
BiblicalUsage: Bûwsh is the word for being ashamed, the paling of the face when sin or failure is exposed, and it also carries the sense of being disappointed or delayed. It runs through Scripture from the garden, where the man and his wife were naked and not ashamed, to the prophets, where God promises His people shall not be ashamed. Shame is the Bible's word for what sin does to a face, and for what God takes away.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe shame is real, and I believe God is the one who removes it. He does not leave His people in the pale-faced fear of being found out; He covers them, and the promise stands that those who trust Him will not be put to shame.
